name: Bolivia: La Paz & Uyuni Salt Flats

cities.base: Central La Paz, close to the witches' market and easy transport to Valle de la Luna, so you're not moving hotels for a two-night stay either side of the flight.
cities.name: La Paz

cities.base: Uyuni town or a salt hotel on the flat's edge, the only credible base for the train cemetery, the salt flat sunset, and the reserve tour departure.
cities.name: Uyuni

cities.base: Day trip from La Paz, no beds here.
cities.name: Valle de la Luna

cities.base: Basic reserve refuge near Laguna Colorada, around 4,300m, no heating, cold showers, only used because the reserve circuit can't be done in a single day from Uyuni.
cities.name: Laguna Colorada refuge

cities.base: Day trip from the Colorada refuge as part of the reserve circuit, no beds here.
cities.name: Laguna Verde

places.name: Muela del Diablo
places.note: A rock tooth formation visible from much of southern La Paz with a real hike to its base, 2 to 3 hours round trip. Only worth adding if Valle de la Luna day is otherwise light, it needs a taxi to the trailhead and some altitude tolerance.

places.name: Mirador Valle de la Luna viewpoint
places.note: A short rise just off the main loop with a wider view over the formations, inside the site's 09:00 to 17:00 hours. Older listings say the Valle de la Luna ticket covers it, unverified, so check the price.

places.name: Valle de la Luna
places.note: Eroded clay and sandstone spires south of the city on a marked loop trail, about 45 minutes. Entry was 30 BOB ($2.55) in October 2026, open 09:00 to 17:00; worth seeing once, not a full morning.

places.name: Plaza Arce and clock tower
places.note: The town's small central plaza, nothing remarkable but a fine place to sit with a coffee before an early tour departure or after a late return.

places.name: Minuteman Revolutionary Pizza
places.note: Long-running pizza place inside Hotel Tonito, the reliable dinner after a cold salar day. A 45cm large is 80 BOB ($6.79) plus 10 per topping, mostly cash; closed Tuesday, and listed hours vary, so go before 20:45.

places.name: Mercado Uyuni (municipal market)
places.note: Basic almuerzo stalls, soup and a plate of rice and meat for a few bolivianos. Not scenic, just a cheap real meal before or after a tour day.

places.name: Cementerio de Trenes
places.note: Rusting 19th century British-built locomotives from the Antofagasta line, 2.5 km southwest of town, free and open all day. Fine on the way out to the salar, not worth a special trip on its own.

places.name: Salar de Uyuni
places.note: The white-out flat itself, about 23 km north near Colchani, free and bundled into any tour. Sunset is when the mirror effect and colors happen, but it gets cold fast once the sun is gone, so bring layers.

places.name: Tiwanaku ruins
places.note: UNESCO site since 2000, a city of 10,000+ people at its height around AD 375 to 700, 1.5 to 2 hours each way. 80 BOB ($6.79) for foreigners covers four sites, open 08:00 to 17:00 daily; prices undated, check.

places.name: Valle de la Luna extended trail loop
places.note: Skip the full marked trail loop beyond the main viewpoint, it's the same eroded clay repeated for another 40 minutes with no new payoff.

places.name: Kilimanjaro Restaurant
places.note: Simple pizza and pasta spot in Uyuni town, useful on the night before or after the reserve circuit when nobody has energy for anything ambitious.

places.name: Popular Cocina Boliviana
places.note: Sit-down Bolivian classics, quinoa soup and llama steak, in a room that is not a tourist stage set. Lunch only, 12:00 to 14:30, closed Sunday; 110 to 120 BOB a head in 2026.

places.name: Gustu
places.note: Gaston Acurio backed restaurant built on all-Bolivian ingredients; the tasting menu is the reason to book. Lunch 12:30 to 14:30, dinner from 18:00 to 21:00 (20:30 Saturday), closed Sunday and Monday; price not confirmed, check.

places.name: Mercado Lanza
places.note: Everyday produce and almuerzo market, not styled for visitors, a $3-4 set lunch here beats any tourist restaurant for value.

places.name: Plaza Murillo
places.note: Government palace, cathedral and legislature around a public square ringed with pigeons, open 24 hours, no gate and no charge. Worth a walk-through on the way to the witches' market, nothing to linger over.

places.name: Museo de la Coca
places.note: Small museum on the coca leaf's role in Andean culture and the drug trade, cheap context for the leaf sold everywhere. About $1.50 to $2, 45 minutes; closed Sunday and over lunch, 13:00 to 14:00.

places.name: Basilica de San Francisco
places.note: 17th century church anchoring the plaza of the same name; the mestizo baroque facade is the reason to look up, the interior is plainer. Church 10:00 to 18:00, closed Sunday; the museum is guided visits only and its hours conflict, check.

places.name: Mi Teleférico (Red Line, La Paz-El Alto cable car)
places.note: Cable car network doubling as public transit, the best views of the city bowl and El Alto rim without a hike. The Red Line runs 06:00 to 23:00 Monday to Saturday, 07:00 to 21:00 Sunday; cheap, fast, genuinely useful.
places.neighborhood: Multiple stations, start at Estacion Central

places.name: Laguna Verde
places.note: Green from mineral content, only shows color in wind and right light, sometimes a letdown if the day is still.
places.neighborhood: Eduardo Avaroa reserve, near Chile border

places.name: Sol de Mañana geysers
places.note: Best at dawn when they're most active, strong sulfur smell, go early or skip.

places.name: Laguna Colorada
places.note: Red algae-stained water and flamingos, covered by the 150 BOB reserve fee paid at the gate. Genuinely worth the discomfort of getting there.

places.name: Mercado de las Brujas
places.note: Dried llama fetuses and coca leaf stalls, more interesting than beautiful. Listed 09:30 to 22:00 daily, but many stalls shut around 17:00 to 18:00, so go in the afternoon.

places.name: Refugio Laguna Colorada check-in and rest
places.note: Shared rooms, thick blankets provided but no heating, cold showers if any water at all. Arrive with headache or nausea common at this altitude after the geyser field, this is where you just rest, not a place to expect comfort.

places.name: Early departure for Sol de Mañana geysers
places.note: Tours leave the refuge before sunrise, around 4:30-5am, to reach Sol de Mañana while the geysers are most active and before other groups arrive. Freezing cold in the dark, but the timing is non-negotiable if you want the geysers steaming rather than dormant.

places.name: Termas de Polques
places.note: Small thermal pool most tours stop at after the geysers, 30 BOB ($2.55). Optional: the water is lukewarm by the time big groups arrive, changing space is minimal, and stripping at 4,400m in freezing wind eats into the drive to Laguna Verde.

places.name: Vizcacha colony near Laguna Colorada
places.note: Rabbit-like rodents sunning on the rocks near the refuge, drivers usually point them out unprompted. Not a destination on its own, just worth having your camera ready during the morning walk.

places.name: Eduardo Avaroa reserve entrance checkpoint
places.note: Where your guide pays the Eduardo Avaroa reserve fee, 150 BOB ($12.73) through 2026, covering Laguna Colorada, Sol de Mañana and Laguna Verde. A few minutes of paperwork at a basic ranger post, not a sight in itself.

places.name: Altiplano drive between geysers and Laguna Colorada
places.note: The 4WD track itself crosses open high desert at over 4,500m with volcanoes on the horizon. No stops planned here, it's the transit, but it's some of the most striking scenery of the whole reserve day and photos happen through the window.

places.name: Refuge stargazing, Laguna Colorada
places.note: No light pollution at 4,300m, southern sky is dense with stars on a clear night. Step outside after dinner, it's brutally cold so don't linger long without layers, no telescope or guide provided, just look up.

places.name: Siloli Desert rock formations
places.note: Driest part of the Atacama-adjacent altiplano, wind-carved rock outcrops scattered across red sand, the Arbol de Piedra is the famous one here but the surrounding formations are worth the driver stopping for.

places.name: James's and Andean flamingo viewing, Laguna Colorada
places.note: Three flamingo species winter here including the rare James's flamingo. No boardwalk or barrier, you view from the shore with your group, binoculars help if you have them.

places.name: Refugio Laguna Colorada communal dinner
places.note: Included in the tour price, cooked by your driver-guide's crew. Basic soup and a main, thin walls, no heating, everyone eats together because there is nowhere else to go. Bring your own snacks if you're picky.

places.name: Arbol de Piedra
places.note: Wind eroded rock standing alone in the desert, shaped like a stone tree. Everyone stops here on the way between Laguna Colorada and Laguna Verde, five minutes to see it and the rest is photos.

places.name: Valle de las Ánimas
places.note: Taller, sharper spires than Valle de la Luna further out, with a real hiking trail through them; listed 07:00 to 18:00 daily, a natural area, so treat that loosely. Worth a free half day, otherwise redundant with Valle de la Luna.

places.name: Café del Mundo Mallasa
places.note: Small coffee stop close to the valley entrance, a place to warm up before the drive back into central La Paz. Nothing remarkable but reliable and quiet.

places.name: Mirador Killi Killi
places.note: City viewpoint in Villa Pabon over the whole bowl of La Paz to Illimani, free and open all day. Best in clear afternoon light; skip it when it is cloudy, the mountain is the point.

places.name: Teleférico Línea Amarilla to Mallasa
places.note: One of La Paz's cable car lines, useful as transport toward Valle de la Luna with views over the canyon on the way down. Cheap and fast, better than the traffic on the road below.

places.name: Puente de Animas rock formations
places.note: Similar eroded badlands terrain on the way between the city and Mallasa, visible from the road, a stop for those who want a second look at the geology without paying a second entry fee.

places.name: Restaurante Casa de Campo
places.note: Bolivian country cooking near the valley, a reasonable lunch stop after the walk before heading back into the city. Portions are large, service can be slow on weekends.

places.name: Zoológico Municipal Vesty Pakos
places.note: Skip. Small municipal zoo near Mallasa, enclosures are dated and it adds nothing that the valley or the city itself doesn't do better.

places.name: Mallasa village center
places.note: Small residential center a few minutes from Valle de la Luna, a place to sit down away from the tour buses. Nothing to seek out on its own.

places.name: Kactus Restaurant
places.note: Bolivian set menus and llama steak on Av Bolivar, open all year from 07:00 to 22:00, so it also does breakfast before a tour. About 50 BOB ($4.24) a head in 2026, with the llama steak around 85.

places.name: La Chapaquita Churrasqueria
places.note: The grill house locals rate highest in town; order the mixed barbecue, 99 BOB ($8.40) in April 2026. Closed Tuesday, dinner from 16:00 (Friday to Sunday from 12:00), Wednesday it shuts at 21:30.

places.name: The Hot Spot Uyuni
places.note: Bolivian dinners on Calle Colon with near-perfect reviews, 17:30 to 21:30, closed Monday. Budget about 150 BOB ($12.73) a head, an undated figure, so check.

places.name: Colchani salt processing and salt museum
places.note: The village on the salar's edge where salt is dried in pyramids and bagged by hand; the small salt-sculpture museum is free, the processing visit 10 BOB ($0.85), 09:00 to 17:00. Most tours stop here first, 45 minutes.

places.name: Playa Blanca salt hotel and Dakar monument
places.note: The old salt hotel, now closed to overnight guests, with the Dakar rally monument and the row of national flags beside it. The monument is free, the hotel's fee is not stated, check the price; 45 minutes.

places.name: Pulacayo
places.note: Huanchaca silver mine town founded in 1833, on UNESCO's tentative list since 2003, with the El Chiripa locomotive and the train Butch Cassidy robbed. Village entry 10 BOB ($0.85), undated; hours vary, check; 90 minutes.

places.name: MUSEF, Museo Nacional de Etnografia y Folklore
places.note: Bolivia's ethnography museum in the Palacio Marques Villaverde; do not miss 3000 Years of Textiles and the Chipaya rooms. 35 BOB ($2.97), 90 minutes, weekdays 08:30 to 16:30 and weekends 09:00 to 13:00 only.
places.neighborhood: Casco Viejo, two blocks from Plaza Murillo

places.name: Museo Nacional de Arte
places.note: Colonial and Bolivian art on Plaza Murillo, 35 BOB ($2.97), cash only, about 75 minutes. Weekdays 08:30 to 16:30, Saturday 09:00 to 17:00, Sunday mornings only until 13:00.

places.name: Casa de Murillo
places.note: Home of independence leader Pedro Domingo Murillo on Calle Jaen; one 20 BOB ($1.70) ticket covers it and three more Calle Jaen museums. Shut 12:30 to about 15:00 on weekdays, closed Monday; Sunday hours conflict, check.

places.name: Museo de Metales Preciosos
places.note: Pre-Columbian gold, silver and copper, Tiwanaku pieces among them, on Calle Jaen. Same shared 20 BOB ($1.70) ticket and hours as Casa de Murillo: closed Monday and shut over the weekday lunch break.

places.name: Museo de Instrumentos Musicales
places.note: Rooms of Bolivian and Andean instruments by Calle Jaen, open weekday mornings only, 09:00 to 13:30. About 5 BOB ($0.42), a 2019 figure, so check the price.

places.name: Palacio Quemado
places.note: Built in 1853, torched by rebels in 1875 (hence the Burnt Palace) and the presidential residence until 2018; in 1946 President Villarroel was hanged from a lamppost in the plaza. Free to view outside, 30 minutes.

outings.why: Eroded clay formations worth seeing once but not lingering, paired with the coca-and-llama-fetus stalls of the witches' market on the way back into town.
outings.name: Valle de la Luna and witches' market loop

outings.why: Rusting British-built locomotives 2.5 km out of town, free, then the salt flat near Colchani for sunset; it turns cold fast once the sun drops.
outings.name: Train cemetery and salt flat sunset

outings.why: The 3-day jeep tour ($100 to $323 pp in 2026): Isla Incahuasi on the salar (30 BOB), Laguna Hedionda, the Siloli desert and Arbol de Piedra, then Laguna Colorada and a night at 4,300m in an unheated refugio.
outings.name: Salar, Isla Incahuasi and Laguna Colorada
outings.fallback: When wind closes the higher tracks, drivers use Laguna Hedionda, lower and more sheltered, with flamingos.

outings.why: Out of the refugio around 05:00 for the Sol de Mañana geysers at about 5,000m, Polques hot springs (30 BOB), Laguna Verde under Licancabur, then the long drive back to Uyuni. Reserve fee is 150 BOB ($12.73).
outings.name: Sol de Mañana, Polques and Laguna Verde
outings.fallback: If Laguna Verde is flat and grey, the geysers at dawn still carry the day.

destination.name: Bolivia: La Paz & Uyuni Salt Flats
destination.pitch: La Paz is the necessary bookend, the salt flats and high desert reserve are the actual trip, and altitude runs the whole show.
destination.caveat: You're pushing past 4,300-4,800m in the reserve on the tail end of the trip, least acclimatized, hours from any oxygen or fast descent if it goes wrong. Prices use 11.79 bolivianos to the dollar; the peg ended in June 2026 and the rate moves. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.nature: The salt flat's white-out horizon and the reserve's red and green mineral lagoons with flamingos are the whole reason to fly this far.
because.culture: The witches' market's coca stalls and dried llama fetuses are a blunt look at Andean folk ritual, not a polished museum version of it.
because.adventure: Two nights above 4,300m in a heated-only-by-blankets refuge, with a 10-12 hour 4WD day in between, is its own kind of adventure.
because.exploration: The Eduardo Avaroa reserve is a two-day 4WD push through geyser fields and desert rock formations most travelers never reach.
